description: GRAIN (Global Registry of Agricultural Irrigation Networks) is a geospatial dataset of surface-water irrigation canals produced by Suresh and Hossain at the University of Washington from OpenStreetMap waterways, using a Random Forest classifier trained on 20,000 samples to separate canals from rivers and streams. It identifies over 3.8 million km of agricultural irrigation canals in 95 countries, with tags that assign canal use. Coverage is global, with the densest mapping in Europe, South and Southeast Asia and North America. The country-scale data are a free download from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0, with the Python code also on Zenodo and a data descriptor in Earth System Science Data (2026). Caveats: completeness follows OpenStreetMap contributions and differs by region, especially for secondary and tertiary canals; median recall on independent validation was about 93.6 % for primary canals, with a mean positional offset of about 98 m. Simulation uses: the delivery network from dams and rivers to farms for irrigation supply, conveyance loss and drought studies. Related records: the FAO global map of irrigation areas (data-fao-global-map-of-irrigation-areas) and the Treasure Valley canal network (data-treasure-valley-idaho-irrigation-canal-network).
